auditSample.displayText: 🎩 FROM A FASHION HOUSE TO A CAFÉ [ POST 2 ] cafe_konditorei_sluka In 1909, Friedrich Ohmann was commissioned to redesign the premises of Ludwig Zwieback & Bruder, an elegant women’s fashion store at the corner of Kärntner Straße and Weihburggasse. His desigb expressed the sophistication of the business, whose customers included wealthy bourgeois and aristocratic women. He subsequently became the company’s regular architect and planned further alterations. Parts of this department-store decoration survive within today’s Sluka. ☕️ In 1922, the Art Nouveau Café Zwieback, designed by Friedrich Ohmann, opened on the ground floor. In 1933, it became the restaurant "Zu den drei Husaren". During alterations in the 1970s, a suspended ceiling was installed at approximately 2.5 metres, concealing much of the decoration above it rather than destroying it. When the premises were renovated for their new life as Sluka, workers removed plasterboard and the suspended ceiling and discovered surviving stucco, decorative figures and glazed roofing. Architect Andreas Call described the discovery as finding a hidden treasure. Surviving fragments of glass and fabric helped guide the restoration of the historic decoration. #wienercafe #wiencafe #viennarestaurants #1000thingstodoinvienna #viennaelegance
